items.stem: A category has high supply risk but low spend. Where does it sit on the Kraljic matrix and what is the usual aim?

options.text: Bottleneck: secure supply continuity and reduce dependence
options.rationale: Correct: high risk/low spend is the bottleneck quadrant, where continuity matters more than price.

options.text: Leverage: drive price down with competition
options.rationale: Leverage is high spend/low risk, not this profile.
Non-critical items are low risk and low spend.
Strategic items are high spend and high risk.

items.explanation: Correct: high risk/low spend is the bottleneck quadrant, where continuity matters more than price.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: You are comparing two suppliers on total cost of ownership rather than price. Which TWO costs belong in the TCO comparison? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: landed cost components are part of TCO.

options.text: Cost of quality failures and rework
options.rationale: Correct: quality and failure costs are a core TCO element.
A third party's list price is not a cost you incur.
Unit price alone is exactly what TCO is meant to go beyond.

items.explanation: Correct: landed cost components are part of TCO.

items.stem: In negotiation planning, what does a strong BATNA most directly give the buyer?

options.text: A credible walk-away alternative that anchors acceptable terms
options.rationale: Correct: a strong BATNA sets the threshold below which no deal is better than this deal.

options.text: A guarantee the supplier will lower price
options.rationale: A BATNA informs your position but guarantees nothing from the supplier.
A BATNA does not replace structured evaluation.
Term length is a separate negotiated variable.

items.explanation: Correct: a strong BATNA sets the threshold below which no deal is better than this deal.
